title: The Uncharted Horizon
premise: Petra Sterling, a bush pilot drowning in debt, ferries a dying prospector named Elias Vane out of the interior; in exchange for the flight, he leaves her a hand-drawn map to a lost survey cache and a promise she must keep: deliver it to his estranged daughter before the mining concession permits expire and erase any legal claim. Pursued by a rival concession company's enforcers who want the map destroyed, Petra crashes in monsoon country and must finish the journey by river with a leaking boat and the reluctant help of Marisol Vane, the daughter who never knew her father. As floodwaters rise and the enforcers close in, Petra discovers the map also documents her own father's disappearance decades ago, forcing her to choose between the inheritance of money and the inheritance of truth. In the end, they reach the land office hours before the permits lapse, file the claim in both families' names, and Petra finally stops running from who she is.
about_author: Rosalind Winterbourne is a former floatplane dispatcher who spent six years in remote northern outposts before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people whose pasts refuse to stay buried.

chapters.title: Fuel and Fog
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A routine medicine run ends with a repo agent waiting at her strip: three payments behind on her de Havilland. She takes a risky charter instead—a gaunt prospector, Elias Vane, coughing blood, who pays double for silence. The beat is desperation dressed as competence.

chapters.title: The Passenger Who Knew Her Name
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Mid-flight, Elias mentions her father's name—Sterling—and a survey expedition that vanished in '89. Petra denies everything, but her hands shake on the yoke. Emotional beat: the past tapping on the windshield glass.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They land at a mission outpost where Elias is clearly dying. He trades her an oilcloth-wrapped map for one promise: take it to his daughter before the concession permits expire in five weeks. Beat: a bargain made under a tarp in the rain.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Small Life
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with flashback fragments. Alone at her shack, she studies the map and finds her father's initials among the original survey crew. She owes money, but now she owes a dead man too. Beat: grief resurfacing as stubbornness.

chapters.title: Men in Clean Boots
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Two men from Halvorsen Concessions visit her strip, asking about a passenger and offering to buy 'any papers' he left. She lies badly. Beat: first contact with the antagonist force; fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Daughter in Port Amara
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV introduced. Marisol Vane, a marine mechanic who hates her father, is tracked down by Petra's telegram. Their first meeting is all friction—Marisol wants nothing from the man who abandoned her. Beat: two guarded women circling the same wound.

chapters.title: What the Oilcloth Hid
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Together they open the map fully: besides the cache coordinates, it records the '89 expedition's true route—including where a second plane went down. Marisol agrees to come, telling herself it's about closure. Beat: reluctant alliance sealed over bad coffee.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They fly out ahead of a building storm system; Halvorsen's floatplane shadows them. Petra flies low through a canyon to lose it and bends a propeller tip landing on a lake. Beat: adrenaline, then the cold math of being grounded.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Stranded lakeside, Marisol patches the prop while Petra confesses the debt, the repo threat, why she stays invisible. Marisol sees her own avoidance mirrored back. Beat: vulnerability traded like currency.

chapters.title: The Downed Plane
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Following the map's old route on foot, they find the wreck of the '89 support plane—and evidence someone stripped it recently, not decades ago. Fresh boot prints. Beat: dread; the race has runners on both sides.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season Opens
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The rains arrive early, flooding their return route to the lake. Their only way forward is downstream: a derelict longboat with a split hull, which Marisol can patch—but barely. Beat: commitment; no going back now.

chapters.title: Leaking Toward the Confluence
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Days on brown water, bailing in shifts, navigating rapids off a sixty-year-old survey sketch. They argue about fathers, forgiveness, and whether promises to the dying bind the living. Beat: intimacy forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The River Village
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They shelter with a river community who remember Elias fondly—and who warn that Halvorsen men passed through, asking questions and leaving threats. An elder gives Petra her father's old letter, mailed years ago and never delivered. Beat: kindness amid danger; the past delivering itself.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Her father's letter reveals he discovered Halvorsen was falsifying survey data to steal indigenous land, and that his disappearance was no accident. Petra realizes the map isn't treasure—it's testimony. Beat: revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Halvorsen's boat traps them in a gorge; there's a chase through rapids, the patched hull tearing, Marisol overboard. Petra hauls her out half-drowned, losing most of their supplies. Beat: physical climax of the middle act; cost made real.

chapters.title: What We Carry
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Huddled under a rock overhang, soaked and short on food, Marisol admits she read the map's margin notes: Elias wrote about both daughters—the one he left and the pilot he watched grow up in mission letters. Beat: grief shared doubles as bond.

chapters.title: The Cache
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach the cache site: not gold, but the original 1989 field journals, photographs, and a signed affidavit naming Halvorsen's fraud. Elias had spent his life guarding it. Beat: the inheritance revealed as truth, not wealth.

chapters.title: Permits Expiring
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Four days remain before the concession claim lapses and the land reverts—unless a counter-claim with documentation is filed. Port Amara is six days away by road, three if the storm breaks. Beat: ticking clock engaged at full volume.

chapters.title: The Long Road
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Hitching rides on logging trucks, evading a checkpoint, Marisol forging a fuel chit, Petra trading her father's compass to a trucker for the last leg. Beat: sacrifice of the last relic of her old identity to secure the new one.

chapters.title: Land Office at Dawn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax: Halvorsen's lawyer waits at the registry to file first. Petra and Marisol arrive minutes before closing, journals in hand, and file the counter-claim with the fraud evidence attached—turning the room against Halvorsen publicly. Beat: triumph earned by inches.

chapters.title: Settlements
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Fallout: an inquiry opens, the repo agent mysteriously paid off by an anonymous settlement (implied Elias's estate), and the land is held in trust for the river communities with both families' names on the filing. Beat: justice distributed, debts dissolved.

chapters.title: The Uncharted Horizon
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, final chapter. Weeks later, Petra flies Marisol over the newly protected valley. The compass is gone but her heading is sure; she's no longer invisible, just private. They plan a survey flight of their own. Beat: resolution—an open horizon chosen freely at last.
